newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NAB chief says in favour of bank mergers.
newsitem.headline: NAB chief says in favour of bank mergers.

text.p: National Australia Bank Ltd managing director Don Argus on Friday voiced his support for Australian bank mergers, urging the government to endorse the recommendations of the Wallis inquiry into the financial system.
"It would be unfortunate if they passed up that rare opportunity," Argus said in a speech at Queensland's Griffith University, which had awarded him an honourary degree.

His comments come a day after fellow major bank Westpac Banking Corp appeared to pre-empt the Wallis report, expected to be released next week, by unveiling an agreed A$1.435 billion bid for Bank of Melbourne Ltd.
Australian Treasurer Peter Costello has said a decision on the bid would have to wait until after the Wallis report was tabled.
NAB is viewed as a potential predator should bank ownership limits be lifted after the Wallis report.
Argus said the government wanted to reduce restrictions on mergers between Australian banks and the operation of foreign banks with a view to increasing competition in the banking sector.
"I would obviously support that...Now all of this will require the federal government to respond favourably to the findings of the Wallis inquiry," he said.
He also said the longer term fundamentals for the Australian economy were promising.
